title: Numbered forward-only .sql migration files; one file one transaction; migration runner tool elicited
context: The Postgres ecosystem has multiple migration tools (node-pg-migrate, sqitch, flyway, prisma migrate, drizzle-kit, knex migrations). Each imposes a different filename convention, a different bookkeeping strategy, and a different transaction shape. Blessing one blocks projects that already carry another; blessing none diffuses the shape across the shelf.
decision: The shipped discipline is numbered forward-only .sql migration files under an elicited migrations directory (default ./migrations/). Each filename begins with a monotonically increasing integer that is unique across the directory (001_..., 002_..., 003_...); the file body is engine-native SQL. The in-tree runner applies each file inside its own transaction (BEGIN, run the file body, COMMIT on success or ROLLBACK on error); the runner records applied filenames in a schema_version bookkeeping table it maintains inside the same database. There are no down migrations; a rollback is a new numbered file inverting the earlier change. Which runner tool the project reaches for is elicited on this ADR (bespoke Node runner shipped in the fixture, node-pg-migrate, sqitch, flyway); recommendedDefault is the bespoke Node runner because it holds the fewest opinions and reads the migrations directory directly.
consequences: The project gets a portable migration shape any Postgres client can apply (a plain .sql file with a leading integer). One file one transaction bounds the rollback surface cleanly but forbids atomic schema changes spanning two files; projects combine multi-step changes into one file. Numbered forward-only means the deploy pipeline's rollback story is a new migration, not a down step; the deploy runbook names this. Refusing to bless a runner tool keeps the shelf out of a maintenance stance; the operator picks whichever tool their team already carries and points it at the same directory. Standards trace clause: generic enterprise practice.

alternativesConsidered.name: Bless node-pg-migrate as the shipped runner
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship node-pg-migrate as the v1.0.0 default; the applying project inherits its filename convention, its bookkeeping table shape, and its up/down direction.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: node-pg-migrate is a fine tool but its filename convention differs from sqitch and flyway; blessing it forces a project already on sqitch to migrate their catalogue. The discipline (numbered forward-only, one file one transaction) is what carries between tools; blessing the discipline and eliciting the tool is cheaper for the operator.

alternativesConsidered.name: Allow bidirectional migrations (up and down)
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship the migration shape as pairs of .sql files (001_up.sql, 001_down.sql); the runner applies up in order and down in reverse.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Down migrations are a lie in production. Rolling back a shipped schema change with a down migration is safe only when the change did not add data-carrying columns or drop constraints in a way the down cannot invert. Forward-only migrations make the rollback path explicit (a new numbered file); the operator writes what actually inverts the change rather than trusting a mechanical down.
